Case for buying POOPYBOT now, as honestly as the brief allows:

The strongest signal is the last 15 minutes: 29 buyers against 9 sellers, 11.37 SOL bought versus 2.82 sold, net inflow of 8.55 SOL, and a +57% return on that window. That is real two-sided-looking demand, not just a launch spike. Graduation was clean (2 seconds), and the first two minutes saw 396 buyers and 382 SOL of buying with a sell-to-buy ratio near 1.0, with the top 5 buyers holding only 11.7% of that flow. The top-3 holder share on the curve is 43%, which is high but not extreme for this stage.

The case is weak, though. Bundle share of 88.5% and a launch bot present suggest the early flow was largely engineered, and the 30-minute return is -18% with a 30% drawdown from the high, so the recent bounce may be a dead-cat move. The brief gives no evidence of operator backing or of a real holder base forming. The 15-minute buying is encouraging but thin relative to a 41-SOL pool, and round-trip costs of 1.4-5.1% eat into any short bounce.

Verdict: a modest case exists based on recent net inflow, but it rests on a 15-minute window against heavy bundling and a fading 30-minute trend. Against a base rate of roughly 20

The completer_share of 43.5% means one party carried nearly half the bonding curve, and that is who can exit into any bounce. The 30-minute drawdown of 30.3% and return of -18% show the cluster has already been distributing, while the last-15-minute flow looks like a recent bid (net_flow +8.55 SOL, +57%) that could be the cluster re-entering to lift the chart.

With a pool of only 41.7 SOL, a $20 round trip costing 1.4-5.1% plus slippage leaves little room. Skip.
